transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um… I guess it’s my eating. After my evening class, sometimes I stop for food and it kind of gets out of hand. Like a whole fast-food meal, then candy from a vending machine, and when I get home I’ll have more snacks too. It feels like I’m making up for not eating much earlier in the day.
When you're eating all that food after class, do you feel like you can't stop or control how much you're eating?
Yeah… I guess so. Once I start with the snacks, I’ll tell myself to just close the bag and go to bed, but I don’t. I just keep reaching for more until I feel kind of embarrassed and sick of myself.
After you eat like that, do you ever try to compensate by making yourself sick, using laxatives, or doing extra exercise?
Yeah… a few times. I’ve gone to the bathroom after and made myself throw up. I just got scared that all that food was going to… show on me, I guess.
How often do you find yourself eating a large amount of food in one sitting, like the episodes you described after class?
Um… usually at least once a week. It’s been like that for maybe three months now, mostly after class.
Do these episodes usually happen when you're alone, and do you feel like you’re hiding them from others?
I don’t know… I mean, I don’t really do it around people. I guess I just don’t talk about it. It’s not something I want anyone noticing.
Do you feel distressed about these eating episodes, or have they affected your daily life in any way?

Yeah… I mean, I still get my work done, and my classes too. But I’ve been leaving pretty quick after class. I don’t really hang around with people much anymore. I just feel embarrassed, and I’m usually thinking about getting home.
How often have you made yourself throw up after these eating episodes?
Usually… about once a week. For the last three months or so, there’s been at least one night after class where I overeat and then… make myself throw up.
Besides making yourself throw up, have you used laxatives, diuretics, or done extra exercise to try to balance out the food you ate?

No… not laxatives or anything like that. I haven’t really done extra exercise either. It’s mostly just… a few times after those late-night eating spells, I went to the bathroom and made myself throw up because I was scared it would show on me.
Do you feel like you eat in secrecy or lose control over your eating during these episodes?

Yeah… I guess I do lose control. Once I start with the snacks, I’ll tell myself to just close the bag and go to bed, but I keep reaching for more anyway. Then I feel… embarrassed, and kind of sick of myself.
Do you usually make yourself throw up because you're especially worried about gaining weight or the way your body looks?

Yeah… mostly that. If the scale’s even up a pound the next morning, I get this knot in my stomach. I start thinking people in class are going to look at me like some sloppy old guy who let himself go.
Do you make yourself throw up after most of these eating episodes, or is it something you do only occasionally when you're especially worried about gaining weight?

Only occasionally. It’s not after most of them… just a few times, when I’d eaten late at night and got really worried it was all going to show on me. Then I’d go to the bathroom and make myself throw up.
Can you tell me if you’ve had more of these episodes where you eat a lot in one sitting and feel like you can’t stop, even when you’re not making yourself throw up?

Yeah… that happens. After my evening class, sometimes I’ll stop for food and it turns into, you know, a whole fast-food meal… then candy from the vending machine, and even more snacks when I get home. It feels like I’m making up for not eating much earlier, and I just don’t really stop.
How often do you have these episodes where you eat a lot in one sitting but don’t make yourself throw up afterward?
I’m not really sure… I haven’t kept count. It’s not every day or anything, but it happens sometimes.
During these episodes where you eat a lot in one sitting but don’t make yourself throw up, do you still feel like you can’t control how much you’re eating once you start?

Yeah… I guess so. Once I start with the snacks, I’ll tell myself to just close the bag and go to bed, but I don’t. I keep reaching for more, and then afterward I just feel… embarrassed. Sick of myself, kind of.
How often do you end up making yourself throw up after these episodes where you feel like you can't control your eating?
Usually… maybe once a week. It’s been like that for the last three months or so, after class. I overeat and then… I make myself throw up.

inference_history.note: The patient describes episodes of eating large amounts of food with a sense of lack of control, which supports binge eating features. This is consistent with either binge eating disorder (F50.2) or bulimia nervosa (F50.3). Anorexia nervosa and related diagnoses are less likely given the absence of restrictive eating patterns or concerns about weight or shape as primary drivers.

The patient reports episodes of eating large amounts of food with a sense of lack of control, followed by compensatory behaviors such as self-induced vomiting. These occur at least once a week for the past three months, which supports the continuation of both candidates (F50.2 for bulimia nervosa and F50.3 for binge eating disorder) as the diagnostic picture is not yet fully clear.

The patient reports distress and impairment in social functioning due to the eating episodes. The frequency of binge eating and compensatory behavior (e.g., self-induced vomiting) occurs at least once a week for three months, which supports the criteria for both F50.2 (Bulimia nervosa) and F50.3 (Binge eating disorder). No additional information to rule out either diagnosis was obtained this turn.

The patient reports loss of control over eating, recurrent episodes of binge eating followed by inappropriate compensatory behavior (self-induced vomiting), and significant concern about body weight and shape. These features are consistent with both F50.2 (Anorexia nervosa) and F50.3 (Bulimia nervosa). The absence of regular use of laxatives, diuretics, or excessive exercise rules out some subtypes but does not eliminate the current candidates. No new disorder has been added or ruled out.

The patient meets criteria for both Binge Eating Disorder (F50.2) and Bulimia Nervosa (F50.3). The patient reports recurrent episodes of binge eating with loss of control, eating until uncomfortably full, and eating large amounts when not physically hungry. Additionally, the patient engages in compensatory behaviors (self-induced vomiting) occasionally after some binge episodes and is significantly distressed about body shape and weight. The frequency of compensatory behaviors is not specified as occurring at least once a week, which keeps both diagnoses in consideration.
